note: State park campground beside the park marina and golf course on the Morro Bay estuary, about 1.5 mi south of the town of Morro Bay; the bay shore is a short walk across State Park Road. Some sites are booked through California State Parks' monthly Reservation Draw lottery rather than the usual rolling window. --Claude
summary: parks.ca.gov + ReserveCalifornia API + imagery/3DEP read. 108 units (25 hookup, 30 A + water, no sewer), RVs to 35 ft (every unit 24 ft+), $35 / $50 flat all year, max stay 10, year-round, no closure banner. Stored count 134 -> 108, electric -> 30, high 35 -> 50. Waterfront: bayview not supported by a sightline; RC types every site 'walk to bay' -> coastal walk recommended (upgrade, reported).
flags: WATERFRONT RE-AUDIT (bayview -> coastal walk recommended, an upgrade, so reported not changed): ReserveCalifornia types all 108 units 'Proximity to Water: walk to bay' (none 'bay view'). On Esri imagery the south rows of the Lower Section (~35.3460,-120.8395) sit 25-30 m north of State Park Road behind a dense cypress/eucalyptus belt; past the road lie the park's marina parking lot and the marina basin of Morro Bay, ~70-100 m from the nearest pads, and the salt marsh of the estuary east of the road. The loops are flat at 4-6 m (3DEP), so the road belt screens any sightline - the stored evidence's 'view holds' is not supported. But Morro Bay is a large saltwater bay and the walk to its shore is ~100 m over the park road and the park's own marina lot, with no highway, town or rail between (curation doc: 'The park's own day-use beach, its parking and park roads may lie between'). If AWH prefers not to upgrade, the evidence supports not waterfront rather than bayview. Suggested evidence: 'RC 2026-11-27: every unit Proximity to Water walk to bay; Esri+3DEP: flat loops 4-6 m, road tree belt screens the marina basin 70-100 m S; walk to the bay shore ~100 m over State Park Rd and the park marina lot, no highway/town -> coastal walk.'
